name: Crucible SG-3 'Lighthouse'
description:
A heavy-duty 26.5mm signal launcher designed for emergency and tactical use, firing parachute-suspended illumination flares that burn at 50,000 candela for 40 seconds, visible at distances exceeding 15 kilometers. The Lighthouse is standard equipment for GLMZ emergency services, corporate security patrols, and anyone operating in areas where electronic communications might be jammed or unavailable.

The SG-3's most common unauthorized use is as an improvised incendiary weapon. The illumination flare burns at 1,200 degrees Celsius and will ignite virtually any flammable material on contact. the Gray Zone residents have discovered that firing a Lighthouse flare into a building's ventilation intake fills the structure with burning magnesium — a crude but effective method of rendering a space uninhabitable. Crucible's lawyers have spent considerable effort establishing that the SG-3 is a signaling device and not a weapon, a distinction that becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as the body count rises.
specifications:
caliber: 26.5mm signal
capacity: 1 round
illumination: 50,000 candela, 40-second burn
visibility: 15+ kilometers
flare temperature: 1,200°C
weight: 0.4 kg
length: 220mm
tactical_use: Emergency signaling, area illumination during night operations, and — unofficially — incendiary attacks. Security teams use Lighthouse flares to illuminate pursuit areas and signal for backup. Less scrupulous users fire them into structures, vehicles, and occasionally people.
cultural_context: The Lighthouse occupies a legal gray zone that everyone exploits. It is classified as emergency equipment, so purchasing one requires no permit. It fires a projectile that burns at 1,200 degrees, so using one offensively is attempted murder. The gap between these two facts contains an entire economy of plausible deniability.
known_users: the Gray Zone residents (for various purposes)
story_hooks: A series of arson attacks across the lower tiers have been carried out with Lighthouse flares — fired through windows at 3 AM, each targeting a specific apartment in a specific building. The targets are all witnesses in the same ongoing investigation.

Someone has modified SG-3 flares to carry chemical payloads instead of illumination compounds, turning an unrestricted signaling device into a chemical weapon delivery system that anyone can buy without a permit.

physical_description.visual_profile: A chunky, industrial signal launcher with a pronounced break-action breech. The silhouette is deliberately utilitarian — all function, minimal ergonomic flourish. The barrel dominates the profile, slightly flared at the muzzle to stabilize the large 26.5mm round. It reads as a tool first, a weapon second, though the distinction feels deliberately maintained.
physical_description.dimensions: 220mm overall length, 65mm width at breech, 45mm barrel diameter. The break-action hinge sits at the gun's midpoint, making it compact enough for one-handed operation but substantial enough to feel like serious equipment.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty without being unwieldy — 0.4kg gives it real presence in the hand, distributed toward the muzzle. The weight feels honest, industrial, designed to absorb recoil from the magnesium round's launch force.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel breech and barrel. The polymer is impact-resistant engineering grade, not cheap polymer, with visible stress-relief ridges molded into the body.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel barrel and breech housing. The finish shows deliberate practicality — non-reflective, resistant to glare. High-contact areas show evidence of coating wear, revealing pale polymer beneath.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with steel-silver accents. Safety markings in high-visibility yellow stripe running along the barrel. The Crucible Educational Foundation logo appears in muted white.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with aggressive diamond-pattern texturing. The texture is designed for gloved operation — corporate security gloves, emergency responder gloves, even grimy street-tier work gloves find purchase. The grip extends slightly forward of the trigger guard.
distinctive_features: Prominent break-action hinge with visible lugs
Large muzzle flare with vertical cooling slots
Recessed safety lever just behind the trigger guard, color-coded yellow
Integrated sighting groove machined into the top of the barrel
Pressure-relief vents along the upper polymer body
Magnesium residue staining (brownish discoloration) around the muzzle and vents on used units
Serial number plate on the left side of the breech, stamped rather than laser-etched
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Educational Foundation logo (stylized lighthouse symbol in a circle) printed in white on the right polymer panel. Smaller text below reads 'SG-3 LIGHTHOUSE' in technical sans-serif. The safety marking 'SIGNAL DEVICE' appears in yellow along the barrel — a deliberate legal positioning.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly used. Corpo security units are pristine. Street-tier operators show scuff marks, polymer stress marks from aggressive handling, magnesium burn residue that doesn't fully clean. Many field units have improvised grip wraps or custom sights added by users.
